title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
author: Anthropic
takes: Context rot and an attention budget: more tokens, worse recall. Three tools for long work - compaction (risks losing what matters later), structured notes outside the window (NOTES.md), sub-agents that return 1-2 thousand token summaries; load knowledge just in time by reference.

title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
author: Anthropic
takes: Compaction alone was not enough: each fresh session gets up to speed from a progress file, the git log and a feature list, works one item, commits and writes its progress. Whether specialised agents beat one general agent is left open.

title: Claude Code agent memory frontmatter
author: shanraisshan
takes: Since v2.1.33 a subagent can keep its own MEMORY.md (project scope in .claude/agent-memory/NAME/), its first 200 lines put in its prompt each time: the field writes expertise down per role rather than keeping it in a session; each role's memory is siloed from the others.

title: Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working
author: Walden Yan (Cognition)
takes: A narrower class works: writes stay single-threaded and extra agents contribute intelligence, not actions. Consulting a 'smart friend' works best by sharing a fork of the asker's full context; unstructured swarms of negotiating agents are a distraction.

title: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Architectures
author: Will Fu-Hinthorn (LangChain)
takes: A supervisor that relays every message plays telephone: it scored lower and spent more tokens than agents handing off directly; removing routing chatter from the workers' context closed much of the gap.

title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
author: Zhang et al.
takes: Knowledge kept by rewriting one summary erodes (context collapse) and drifts toward the terse (brevity bias); itemised, incremental additions to a playbook keep the detail. ICLR 2026.

title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
author: Hong, Troynikov, Huber (Chroma)
takes: Models do worse as input grows, even on simple tasks and well below the window's size; focused inputs beat full ones.

title: Exploring Advanced LLM Multi-Agent Systems Based on Blackboard Architecture
author: Han and Zhang
takes: Agents share one blackboard instead of private memories; a control unit picks who acts from what is on it. With 2510.01285 (agents volunteer for requests posted to the board): routing by a shared record, not by a central relay.

title: Sleep-time Compute
author: Letta
takes: Stateful agents keep editable memory blocks; a separate agent rewrites them between tasks into clean, concise learned context, so the working agent need not re-derive it.

title: LAVA glossary: the scheduler
author: Linaro
takes: A single scheduler on the server assigns devices to submitted test jobs; dispatchers run them, one job per device at a time. Jobs queue; nobody touches a board outside the scheduler.

title: LAVA CI - The Mesa 3D Graphics Library
author: Mesa
takes: Mesa's merge requests reach real boards only through the LAVA instance, which schedules jobs onto the boards present.

title: Introduction to CI-tron
takes: A CI gateway service that orchestrates and manages the devices under test: one gateway owns its devices and serves the jobs that come for them.

title: Hardware testing automation: a status update - postmarketOS
takes: postmarketOS's hardware CI runs phones behind a CI-tron gateway - the precedent nearest to a Linux-phone lab.

title: Gas Town: project roles (Refinery: merge queue processor)
author: Steve Yegge
takes: The Refinery is the one agent that merges all changes to main, one at a time; a role, not a session - when a session for the role starts it takes up the next step, nudged by patrols.

title: A Universal Modular ACTOR Formalism for Artificial Intelligence
author: Carl Hewitt, Peter Bishop, Richard Steiger
takes: An actor owns its state alone and others reach it only by messages it takes one at a time: the single-writer principle that keeps shared state free of races.

title: Rust RFC template
author: The Rust project
takes: Every proposal discusses prior art, good and bad, and the alternatives - set against what others did before it is taken.

title: PEP 12 - Sample reStructuredText PEP Template
author: Python
takes: A Rejected Ideas section kept with the proposal; PEP 1's Superseded-By and Replaces for a redo.

title: MADR: Markdown Architectural Decision Records 4.0
takes: Considered options with pros and cons beside every decision; a status that says superseded by which.

title: Extend Claude with skills
author: Anthropic
takes: The description always in context, the body loaded when used; SKILL.md under 500 lines, reference in files read only when needed.

title: Wikipedia:Maintenance
author: Wikipedia
takes: Upkeep is a standing backlog, not a campaign: a page that needs work is tagged (a cleanup template), the tags gather into backlog categories by kind, and anyone takes one and removes the tag when it is fixed - the tag proposes, the fix is the edit.

title: How Claude remembers your project - Claude Code Docs
author: Anthropic
takes: What is loaded every session is kept small: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md, since longer files consume context and reduce adherence; move what matters for only part of the work to rules that load when it is touched; imports organise a file but do not reduce its cost.

title: Tools That Stop AI Agents Using Stale Documentation
author: Unblocked
takes: Agents trust whatever they read: keep them off stale documentation by verification workflows, freshness metadata (when a page was last checked), documentation generated from the code, and weighting by authority.

title: Compaction overview - Claude Platform Docs
author: Anthropic
takes: Compaction replaces older turns with a summary Claude writes; the session goes on, but what is kept is whatever the summary chose.

title: Context engineering: memory, compaction, and tool clearing
author: Anthropic
takes: Three primitives for long-running agents: clearing old tool results that can be fetched again, compaction of the conversation, and a memory of notes kept outside the window. Together they kept a run's peak context at half the baseline and its end at 14k tokens instead of 334k.

title: Gas Town Emergency User Manual
author: Steve Yegge
takes: Use gt handoff liberally after every task, in every worker: sessions are cattle, the role's identity and its hook carry the work to the next session.

title: Claude Code: create custom subagents
author: Anthropic
takes: agents/NAME.md is the role card: model, effort, skills in frontmatter; claude --agent NAME starts a main session as it; plugin agents ignore hooks, mcpServers, permissionMode

title: Claude Code: agent teams
author: Anthropic
takes: teammates may be agent definitions, but their skills are not applied and the lead cannot hand over - not the route for lasting roles yet

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
author: Anthropic
takes: a lead writes each brief (objective, output, tools, boundaries); strong lead, lighter workers: model per role

title: Gas Town: role definitions and gt prime
author: Steve Yegge
takes: each role a small definition plus a template, primed at SessionStart with its work and mail, lighter after compaction

title: CrewAI: agents (role, goal, backstory)
author: CrewAI
takes: a role is a few fields; we keep purpose and leave the backstory out

title: Team Topologies
author: Matthew Skelton, Manuel Pais
takes: a team is its type, owned scope and interaction modes; with RACI's one accountable, the card's owns, never and reports to

title: Claude Code: skills (the skill listing and its budget)
author: Anthropic
takes: every listed skill costs context each turn; skillOverrides off/name-only, skillListingMaxDescChars and disableBundledSkills trim the listing; an agent's skills field only preloads

title: Site Reliability Engineering, ch. 5: Eliminating Toil
author: Google
takes: measure by a rule against a cap; the owners turn what is found into engineering - no standing toil-keeper

title: How we use friction logs to improve the product
author: Resend
takes: the newcomer's own log of friction is cheap signal; the owning team fixes

title: Writing effective tools for agents - with agents
author: Anthropic
takes: read transcripts and evals for tool errors and redundant calls; fix the tool's description or shape

title: Investigating agent trajectories
author: Microsoft
takes: note the first wrong call; bring the evidence to whoever owns the cause; a new skill is the last resort

title: Langfuse: error analysis
author: Langfuse
takes: read traces, cluster first failures, repeat after changes; the domain calls stay with people

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
author: Cemri et al.
takes: a taxonomy of 14 failure modes - system design, misalignment, verification

title: Paper cuts in developer experience
author: Rebecca Murphey
takes: everyone reports small friction; owners fix; the pile becomes data for priorities

title: What agents spend on recording into a tad knowledge base (ikb-friction-and-world)
author: ikb-cli session
takes: 31 transcripts: 41 of 240 tad r calls failed (17%), each failure ~8.4 calls and ~11k tokens; after ikb 0-1 failures in 4 runs at equal tokens - a one-off subagent count, not rerunnable; the method read-weight's struggled-with now repeats by script

title: creation-guidelines/lab-agent (main, 0.1.53)
takes: what ran, when, what depends on it

title: grenudi/lab-agent-jobs: job and board history
takes: what ran, when, what depends on it

title: Agent Skills specification
author: Anthropic, then open
takes: SKILL.md with name and description is read by Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and some 40 others; harness-only keys are not portable

title: AGENTS.md
author: Agentic AI Foundation
takes: one instructions file most harnesses read; Claude Code reads it where no CLAUDE.md is

title: rulesync
author: dyoshikawa
takes: one source generated into many harnesses; its end-of-life list of targets shows what tracking every harness costs

title: 2016 Letter to Shareholders (one-way and two-way doors, disagree and commit)
author: Jeff Bezos
takes: two-way doors decided fast near the work; escalate at once, never by exhaustion; disagree and commit

title: RAPID decision making
author: Bain
takes: one decider for each decision, who holds the accountability; input is not the decision

title: Site Reliability Engineering: Managing Incidents
author: Google
takes: the commander holds every role not delegated; declare early; handoffs are acknowledged

title: Gas Town: escalation design
author: Steve Yegge
takes: a blocked worker escalates and goes on; each tier resolves or forwards; every escalation tracked, re-escalated when stale

title: Claude Code auto mode
author: Anthropic
takes: what still reaches a human: destroying or exfiltrating, weakening security, crossing trust boundaries, affecting others

title: Copilot coding agent: customize the agent firewall
author: GitHub
takes: downloads from allowlisted official sources pass; other hosts are flagged, not asked for

title: SLSA v1.0: Verifying artifacts
author: OpenSSF
takes: check a file's hash or provenance against an expectation from a separate trusted channel before use

title: Site Reliability Engineering: Postmortem Culture
author: Google
takes: a finding becomes an owned, tracked action item in the owner's system - not a note in the incident

title: Double Loop Learning in Organizations
author: Chris Argyris
takes: learning that changes the governing rules, not only the next action - the method itself is revised from what was found

title: postmarketOS: Porting to a new device
author: postmarketOS
takes: a feedback channel and a downstream (vendor) port as the base before mainlining

title: postmarketOS: Mainlining guide
author: postmarketOS
takes: mainline from the nearest supported sibling, one change at a time, with UART, framebuffer or ramoops to see it

title: Claude Code: plugin dependencies
author: Anthropic
takes: a plugin depends on another by a semver range resolved from release tags; names are namespaced; no agent extends another's body

title: Helm: library charts
author: Helm
takes: the overlay pins its base and includes its templates by name, overriding only what differs

title: Google engineering practices: the standard of code review
author: Google
takes: approve what improves the code's overall health; the style guide decides style, design is judged by principles

title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
author: Qian et al.
takes: programmer, reviewer and tester roles beat a bare model; separating review from writing helps

title: Lean Enterprise Institute lexicon: jidoka
author: Lean Enterprise Institute
takes: stop at the first abnormality so its cause shows and is fixed at the root

title: Which incidents need a postmortem?
author: OneUptime
takes: choose reviews by impact and learning value; a repeat of a class or a cluster of minor events is a trigger

title: Incident postmortem template
author: Rootly
takes: a light note for minor incidents, a review for a recurring one; the exposed team does not waive its own review

title: Linux kernel: AI coding assistants
author: Linux kernel developers
takes: an agent never adds Signed-off-by - only a person certifies; the tool is named in a trailer (Assisted-by)

title: GitHub: creating a commit with multiple authors
author: GitHub
takes: Co-authored-by trailers; credit links only to an account's email - the run's name rides the trailer, the account stays the author
